No new ideas today: three short problems on Lecture 10. Do each one alone,
then open "Check your result". Every question on this page has its answer:
try first, then check.

## Recall

- P(A) = outcomes of A ÷ all outcomes, when they are equally likely.
  P(not A) = 1 − P(A). Two independent events: P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B).
- P(A | B): count A only inside B. Without putting back:
  P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B | A).
- E = x₁p₁ + x₂p₂ + …: the long-run average. Fair: the price equals E(win).
  A success with probability p takes 1/p tries on average.

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Recall"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="1/12|0.5"}
One die. What is P(more than 4)?
:   1/3

    Why: 5 and 6: 2 of 6 outcomes.

P(A) = 0.2. What is P(not A)?
:   0.8

    Why: 1 − 0.2.

A drop has p = 1/10. How many tries does it take on average?
:   10

    Why: 1/p = 10.
:::
:::

## Activity 1 · Gems: theory and many rolls

A slime drops a gem when a die shows a 6. Two slimes roll two dice, and the
dice are independent. The designer wants to know how often players get gems,
and checks the code with many rolls.

![Two dice: 36 equally likely outcomes in a grid.](images/dice-sums.png){width=80%}

{{< sim file="sims/roll-lab.html" poster="sims/roll-lab.png" title="Roll Lab: theory and experiment" height="760" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 1 · Theory and rolls · 18 min"}
1. Write the sample space of one die, P(gem) and P(no gem).
2. Two slimes: find P(two gems) and P(at least one gem). Use the complement
   for the second one.
3. Find P(the sum of two dice is 7) with the grid.
4. In **Roll Lab**, roll 10 times, then 1000 times. Write the share of 6s
   (hits ÷ rolls) each time. Then choose "at least one 6 (two dice)" and roll
   1000 times.

*Your product:* four probabilities, three shares, and one sentence: when is
the share close to the probability?

::: {.check}
1. S = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}; P(gem) = 1/6; P(no gem) = 5/6.
2. P(two gems) = 1/6 × 1/6 = 1/36. P(at least one) = 1 − 5/6 × 5/6 =
   1 − 25/36 = 11/36, about 0.31.
3. (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), (6,1): 6/36 = 1/6.
4. After 10 rolls the share of 6s can be far from 1/6 ≈ 0.17 (0.1, 0.3 …).
   After 1000 rolls it is close (about 0.14 to 0.19), and "at least one 6"
   is close to 0.31.

The share comes close to the probability only after many rolls.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Gems"}
A slime drops a gem on a 6. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="1/6|exactly 100"}
What is P(no gem from two slimes)?
:   25/36

    Why: 5/6 × 5/6: the dice are independent.

The game rolls 600 times. About how many gems come?
:   about 100

    Why: 600 × 1/6 = 100, but not exactly: chance moves a little.

After 10 rolls, the share of 6s is 0.4. Is the code wrong?
:   not sure: 10 rolls are too few

    Why: few rolls jump a lot; the share needs many rolls.
:::
:::

## Activity 2 · A critical hit and a chest

A sword makes a critical hit when two dice show a sum of 10 or more.
Sometimes the first die is already known. A chest holds 6 items, 2 of them
rare; the hero takes two, one after the other, without putting one back.

![A condition makes the sample space smaller: count only inside B.](images/conditional-grid.png){width=80%}

{{< sim file="sims/conditional-lab.html" poster="sims/conditional-lab.png" title="Conditional Lab: what do we know already?" height="740" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 2 · Knowing the first die · 18 min"}
1. Find P(critical hit) before the roll: count the sums of 10 or more in the
   grid.
2. The first die shows 5. Find P(critical hit | first die is 5).
3. Check the case "first die is 6" in **Conditional Lab**: A = sum 10 or
   more, B = first die is 6.
4. Find P(two rare items) from the chest.

*Your product:* four probabilities, and one sentence: why does knowing the
first die change the chance?

::: {.check}
1. (4,6), (5,5), (5,6), (6,4), (6,5), (6,6): 6/36 = 1/6.
2. Inside B: (5,1) … (5,6), 6 outcomes; (5,5) and (5,6) give 10 or more:
   2/6 = 1/3.
3. Conditional Lab: P(A | B) = 3/6 = 1/2 ((6,4), (6,5), (6,6)).
4. 2/6 × 1/5 = 2/30 = 1/15: after a rare item, 5 items are left with 1 rare.

The known die removes the outcomes outside B, so we count in a smaller
sample space.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Hits and chests"}
Two dice; a critical hit needs a sum of 10 or more. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="1/36|2/15"}
The first die shows 1. What is P(critical hit)?
:   0

    Why: 1 + 6 = 7 is the most: no sum of 10.

The first die shows 4. What is P(critical hit)?
:   1/6

    Why: only (4, 6) inside the 6 outcomes of B.

A chest has 5 items, 1 rare. The hero takes two without putting back. What is P(the rare one first, then a normal one)?
:   1/5

    Why: 1/5 × 4/4: after the rare item, every item left is normal.
:::
:::

## Activity 3 · Is the crate worth its price?

A crate holds 10 items: 2 are worth 50 coins, 5 are worth 10 coins and 3 are
empty. It costs 18 coins. An axe hits for 12 damage; a critical hit, with
the probability 1/3, does 30. A rare cape drops with the probability 1/20.

![The expected value of a crate: each value times its probability.](images/expected-value.png){width=80%}

{{< sim file="sims/crate-lab.html" poster="sims/crate-lab.png" title="Crate Lab: the expected value of a loot crate" height="800" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 3 · Expected value and price · 18 min"}
1. Find E(coins) of the crate and the expected gain at the price 18. Is it
   fair? Which price is fair?
2. Find E(damage) of the axe per hit.
3. How many tries does the cape take on average?
4. In **Crate Lab**, build the crate (2 × 50, 5 × 10, 3 × 0) with the price
   18. Open 1000 crates and compare the average with your E.

*Your product:* two expected values, one gain, one fair price and one
average wait.

::: {.check}
1. E = 50 × 0.2 + 10 × 0.5 + 0 × 0.3 = 10 + 5 + 0 = 15 coins. Gain =
   15 − 18 = −3 coins: not fair. A fair price is 15 coins.
2. E = 12 × 2/3 + 30 × 1/3 = 8 + 10 = 18 damage.
3. 1/p = 20 tries on average (some players need many more).
4. Crate Lab: after 1000 crates the average is close to 15.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Crates"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="25|41.7"}
A crate gives 30 coins (p = 0.5) or nothing (p = 0.5). What is E?
:   15

    Why: 30 × 0.5 + 0 × 0.5 = 15.

A crate has E = 15 and costs 20. What is the expected gain?
:   −5

    Why: E − price = 15 − 20.

A pet drops with p = 1/50. After 50 tries, does every player have it?
:   no

    Why: 1/p is an average: many players need more tries.
:::
:::

## Wrap-up {.summary}

- You can compute the chance of a drop with the complement and AND, and
  check it with many rolls.
- You can use a known result: count only inside B, and multiply along a
  chest without putting back.
- You can decide with the expected value if a crate is worth its price.
